name: Bookshelf
description: A shelf of book spines; click one and the book flies onto the table, its cover opens with real physics, and the pages turn with real paper geometry. With Esc or a click outside, it goes back to the shelf.
interactionNotes: Go to the spine you want; it rises. Click it and it comes down from the shelf onto the table and its cover opens with a heavy swing on a hinge (you can also drag it up yourself and let go). Drag or click the pages from their outer half; a fast flick turns the page, a half-hearted one springs back. The arrows turn pages (right = next, in step with the page-turn direction of a Persian book) and Escape closes. Clicking outside the book or pressing Escape closes it and it flies back to its place on the shelf; on a wide screen, reaching the last page also closes it. Narrow viewports are single-page.

props.name: books
props.description: The shelf's books (`title`, `author`, `cloth`, `foil`, `blurb`, `content` and optional `height`/`width`/`label`); defaults to the component's own five books with Persian text.

props.name: series
props.description: Series name; the header of the right-hand pages and the foot of each back cover.

props.name: count
props.description: How many of the first books on the shelf are shown; without it all of them, and `0` also means all (not none).

props.name: autoOpen
props.description: Open the first book automatically — for the site's auto preview.

tips: It has no dependencies — not even `motion`; everything is hand-rolled physics on requestAnimationFrame plus pure CSS: covers with a heavy-swing hinge equation, pages with folded-paper geometry (the fold is the perpendicular bisector of the line from the corner to the target).
The geometry is fully mirrored for a Persian book: spine on the right, first page on the left and turning from left to right — not a visual trick; the math itself is mirrored.
Text is paginated with CSS columns and any text of any length paginates correctly by itself; the page numbers are in Persian.

Each book's cover and spine are set with `cloth` and `foil`; the physical colors (cream paper, shelf wood) don't change with the theme but are variables `--bs-*` in `bookshelf.css` — it's a book, but its color is in your hands.
On wide screens it expands as a two-page spread and on phones as single-page; the return to the shelf flies with `offset-path` and until it settles, its spine rotates into the row.
With `prefers-reduced-motion` the book opens without animation and the flights are removed; the pages still turn.
